claim_reviews.conclusion: "Rice cooker" correctly cues an electric appliance for cooking rice.

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct Indonesian term for a rice cooker, including an electric rice-cooking appliance.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: penanak nasi

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct Malaysian Malay term; official and commercial Malaysian usage explicitly applies periuk nasi elektrik to electric rice cookers.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: periuk nasi

claim_reviews.conclusion: Supported as a useful contrast between common Indonesian penanak nasi and Malaysian periuk nasi, but it is not an exclusive one-to-one distinction because shared English usage and additional synonyms exist.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation: different-common-word

claim_reviews.conclusion: No cross-variety false friend affects the learner answer. Malay periuk nasi also has an idiomatic sense of livelihood/source of income, but the appliance sense is clear in this cue.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

rationale: Both local forms are valid and commonly used for rice cookers. The Indonesian term is specifically evidenced for an electric appliance; Malaysian periuk nasi is established for rice cooker, including electric models. The different-common-word relation is useful, though not exclusive because English rice cooker and additional synonyms occur in both varieties. No cross-variety false friend is present; periuk nasi has a separate Malay idiomatic sense meaning livelihood/source of income.
